correctness.rationale: The proof is complete for all integers n>=3. Every C5 column is an independent set of size <=2. An empty column forces all five vertices in each adjacent column; a singleton forces two adjacent selected rows in each adjacent column; both are impossible. Each two-element column has a unique center. Horizontal independence restricts adjacent centers to increments ±1. Two-domination at the two residual unselected row types forces opposite choices of the two neighboring centers, hence a constant signed increment around the entire cyclic second factor. Closure requires 5|n. Conversely all five shifts of either signed slope independently and 2-dominate, and the first two columns recover the parameters uniquely, yielding exactly ten sets of size 2n. Both a direct exhaustive vertex-bitset verifier (n=3..6) and an independent local-column transfer verifier (n=3..40), checked by actual replay, corroborate the boundary cases, not substitute for the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The direct full-text comparison with Bednarz–Wloch, DOI 10.17951/a.2016.70.2.1, pp.4–5, finds Theorem 2.5 asserting that C_m square C_n has a (2-d)-kernel only if m,n are both even or m=n. The fully checked set S_{1,0} on C_5 square C_10 violates that necessity. The new theorem also proves that precisely the multiples of five admit such configurations for this first factor, and classifies all ten patterns. Corollary 2.6 already counts ten for the equal-order C_5 square C_5 case; this is credited. Nagy arXiv:1504.03224 and the 2012/2015 kernel literature do not imply the differing-order classification. Targeted mathematical-record, primary-literature, and historical-claim searches found no covering result, with unindexed-priority risk.
residual_risks: Published corrected versions, unpublished notes, or equivalently formulated independent-dominating-set tables not indexed in the inspected services could already give this exact classification.
The 2015 Ars Combinatoria scanned full text was not comprehensively read page-by-page; its stated scope and inspected sections did not suggest direct coverage.
Research-record retrieval is similarity-ranked and therefore not a mathematical uniqueness or worldwide novelty certificate.

The original 2012 paper is dated by publication year, without a verified calendar day of first public availability; the 2015-04-13 first_public_date is the earliest precisely verifiable public date among the reviewed archival sources.

value.rationale: The exact infinite-family classification exposes a concrete mathematical error in a published necessary-and-sufficient criterion (Bednarz–Włoch 2016 Theorem 2.5), furnishing infinitely many unequal-order counterexamples and a sharp period-five structural characterization. Such correction is an intrinsic motivated gap in 2-dominating kernel theory, beyond a routine isolated finite example. The already published equal-order count is not claimed as novel; the retained result is the complete mixed-size classification and corrected necessity on this natural fixed-width toroidal family.
